entry: Genus of bushy, tuberous, herbaceous perennial plants native to Mexico and Central America, in the daisy family [[Asteraceae]]. Relatives include the sunflower, [[Chrysanthemum|chrysanthemum]] and zinnia. Dahlias were known only to the Aztecs and other peoples of southern North America until the Spanish conquest, after which the plants were brought to Europe. Garden dahlias are octoploids, with eight sets of [[Chromosome|chromosomes]], and many transposons contribute to their great diversity of forms. Over 50,000 [[Cultivar|cultivars]] have been developed through [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridization]], mainly from *D. pinnata*, *D. coccinea* and *D. variabilis*. Dahlia is the national flower of Mexico. The tubers of some varieties are of medicinal and dietary value, storing inulin, a polymer of [[Fructose|fructose]], instead of starch.

Mild-flavored winter [[Radish|radish]] (*Raphanus sativus* var. *longipinnatus*) with a long, white, cylindrical root. Native to continental [[East Asia]], daikon is now harvested and eaten worldwide. The name is Japanese for big root; in parts of South Asia it is called mooli, and in [[Chinese cuisine]] it is usually called white radish. Roots typically measure 25–50 cm and weigh 0.45–0.9 kg. They have a crisp texture and less pungency than smaller radishes, and Chinese and Indian varieties tolerate higher temperatures than Japanese ones. In some places daikon is left unharvested to loosen compacted soil and recover nutrients; in [[North America]] it is grown mainly as a fallow crop. The root is rich in [[Vitamin C|vitamin C]] and potassium.

British daily middle-market tabloid newspaper, with a conservative editorial stance, founded in 1896 and published in London. The paper is owned by the Daily Mail and General Trust, whose chairman is Jonathan Harmsworth, 4th Viscount Rothermere. Its average daily circulation was 1.13 million copies in February 2020, and women make up a majority of its readers. Ted Verity became editor in November 2021. Critics have cited its sensationalist and inaccurate scare stories about science and medical research, and instances of plagiarism.

Place where milk is stored and where butter, cheese and [[Yogurt|yogurt]] are made or sold. The word also describes a dairy farm, or the part of a mixed farm devoted to milk from [[Cattle|cows]], buffaloes, [[Goat|goats]], yaks, sheep, horses or camels. A dairy farm produces milk, and a dairy factory processes it into products; together they form the global dairy industry, part of the [[Food industry|food industry]]. Milk-producing animals were domesticated thousands of years ago, initially as part of the subsistence farming of [[Nomad|nomads]]. With industrialization, milk became a commercial industry with specialized dairy breeds of cattle. The word comes from Old English for female servant, as milking was historically done by dairymaids.

Capital and largest city of [[Senegal]] (metropolitan pop., 2023: 4.0 million), on the Cap-Vert peninsula, the westernmost point of mainland Africa. The Portuguese established a base on the island of Gorée, which was used for the [[Atlantic slave trade]]. France took the island in 1677 and, after annexing the mainland in the 19th century, Dakar grew into a major port and a city of the [[French colonial empire]]. In 1902 it replaced Saint-Louis as capital of French West Africa, and it became capital of independent Senegal in 1960. Dakar hosted the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics, becoming the first city in Africa to host an Olympic sporting event.

Spiritual head of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism. Altan Khan conferred the title in 1578 on Sonam Gyatso, who became the 3rd Dalai Lama. From 1642 to 1951 the Dalai Lamas led the government of [[Tibet]]. The [[14th Dalai Lama|14th]] Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, fled to India during the 1959 Tibetan uprising and lives in exile in Dharamshala. Historians disagree over the extent of the Dalai Lamas' secular power. Some describe a priest-patron relationship with Mongol, Manchu and Chinese rulers, while critics argue that it obscured the dominance of more powerful states.

Indian singer, songwriter and record producer. Born in Patna, Bihar, into a Punjabi Sikh family, he helped popularize bhangra worldwide. His debut album, *Bolo Ta Ra Ra*, sold over 20 million copies, and his 1998 song "Tunak Tunak Tun" became an international success. In 2018 he was convicted in a human trafficking case that originated in 2000 and sentenced to two years' imprisonment. He has denied wrongdoing.

Sub-provincial port city in Liaoning province, China (pop., 2020: 7,450,785), at the southern tip of the Liaodong peninsula. It is Liaoning's second-largest city after the provincial capital, [[Shenyang]], and the southernmost city in Northeast China. The [[Russian Empire]] built a commercial town there after leasing the area from the [[Qing dynasty]] in 1898. After the [[Russo-Japanese War]] of 1904–1905, Japan occupied the area as the Kwantung Leased Territory and called the city Dairen. In 1950 the city merged with Lüshun to form Lüda, and it took the name Dalian again in 1981. Today it is a financial, shipping and logistics center for [[East Asia]]. It is one of the world's top 40 science cities by the Nature Index, ranking 37th in 2023, and it is home to Dalian University of Technology and Dalian Maritime University.

Term for the lowest stratum of the castes in the [[Indian subcontinent]], also called Harijans. The word comes from a Sanskrit term meaning broken or scattered. Dalits were excluded from the four varnas of Hindu society and were seen as forming a fifth. The term was popularized by [[B. R. Ambedkar]], himself a Dalit, who drafted the [[Constitution of India]]. The Constitution lists Dalits as Scheduled Castes, entitling them to affirmative action known in India as reservation. Most Dalits follow [[Hinduism]], though significant numbers follow [[Buddhism]], [[Sikhism]], [[Christianity]] or [[Islam]].

City in northern [[Texas]], United States (pop., 2020: 1.3 million). The ninth-most populous U.S. city, it is the seat of Dallas County and the core city of the [[Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex]], the fourth-largest U.S. metropolitan area. Founded as a settlement in 1841 by John Neely Bryan, Dallas grew with railroads serving cotton, cattle and later oil. The [[Interstate Highway System]] made it a major transportation hub. Its economy centers on financial services, defense, information technology and telecommunications. Eleven of the metroplex's 23 Fortune 500 companies are located within city limits. President [[John F. Kennedy]] was assassinated in Dallas on November 22, 1963.

Professional American football team in the [[Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex]], competing in the [[National Football League]]. The team joined the NFL as an expansion team in 1960 and has played at AT&T Stadium in Arlington since 2009. It has made eight [[Super Bowl]] appearances, and its streak of 190 consecutive sellouts began in 2002. [[Forbes]] has ranked the team the most valuable sports franchise in the world since 2016, and it was valued at about $13 billion as of late 2025.

Conurbation in north [[Texas]], United States, centered on [[Dallas]] and Fort Worth (pop., 2020: 7,637,387). Officially the Dallas–Fort Worth–Arlington metropolitan statistical area, it is the most populous in Texas and the fourth-largest in the United States. Its economy centers on banking, insurance, telecommunications, technology, energy and logistics, and it hosts 23 Fortune 500 companies as of 2022. The name metroplex, a blend of metropolis and complex, is credited to advertising executive Harve Chapman. In 2016 the area had the highest annual population growth in the United States, and it had an estimated 8,344,032 residents in 2024.

American prime time [[Soap opera|soap opera]] broadcast on [[CBS]] from 1978 to 1991. It followed the feuding Ewing family of Texas, owners of the oil company Ewing Oil and the Southfork ranch. Oil tycoon J. R. Ewing, played by [[Larry Hagman]], became its breakout character. Its cliffhangers included the "Who shot J.R.?" mystery, and the 1980 episode "Who Done It" remains the second-highest-rated primetime telecast ever. The show ran 357 episodes over 14 seasons and won four Emmy Awards. In 2007 [[Time (magazine)|Time]] included it in its list of "100 Best TV Shows of All-Time."

Standard unit of mass for atomic-scale entities, symbol Da, defined as 1/12 of the mass of an unbound neutral [[Carbon|carbon-12]] [[Atom|atom]] at rest in its ground state. Also called the unified atomic mass unit (symbol u), it is used in physics and chemistry to express the masses of atoms, [[Molecule|molecules]] and particles. A [[Proton|proton]] has a mass of about one dalton. The name was proposed by IUPAC in 1993 and honors English chemist and physicist [[John Dalton]]. The molar mass of a substance in grams per mole is numerically equal to the average mass of one of its molecules in daltons: one mole of [[Water|water]] weighs about 18.0153 grams, and one water molecule weighs about 18.0153 Da. Proteins are measured in kilodaltons (kDa) and megadaltons (MDa).

Monetary award in [[Common law|common law]] paid to a claimant as compensation for loss or injury. To warrant an award, the claimant must show that a breach of duty caused foreseeable loss involving property damage or physical or mental injury; pure economic loss is rarely recognized. Compensatory damages are divided into special damages, such as lost earnings, property damage and medical expenses, and general damages, such as pain and suffering and emotional distress. Damages may instead be nominal, contemptuous or exemplary. Recovery is subject to the principle of proximate cause. In [[Contract|contract]] law, expectation damages put the injured party in the position it would have occupied without the breach.

Capital and largest city of [[Syria]], known as the City of Jasmine. First settled in the 3rd millennium BC, it is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world and was the capital of the [[Umayyad Caliphate]] from 661 to 750. After the Abbasid victory, the seat of Islamic power moved to [[Baghdad]], and the city's importance declined until the Ayyubid, Mamluk and Ottoman periods. Damascus lies on a plateau 680 metres above sea level in the eastern foothills of the Anti-Lebanon range, and the Barada River flows through it. Patterned silks sold there, at a Western terminus of the [[Silk Road]], gave English the word damask. During the [[Syrian civil war]] it was named the least livable of 140 global cities in a global liveability ranking.

Port city and capital of Damietta Governorate, Egypt, on the Damietta branch of the [[Nile]] Delta. It lies 15 km from the [[Mediterranean Sea]] and about 200 km north of [[Cairo]]. Known as Tamíathis in the [[Hellenistic period]], it was a focus of the Crusades. Crusaders captured it in November 1219, after a siege in which only 3,000 of its 70,000 inhabitants survived. [[Louis IX of France|Louis IX]] took it in 1249, but after his capture in 1250 he surrendered Damietta as ransom. The Mamluks destroyed the city in 1250, and a new town was founded to the south. Damietta joined the [[UNESCO]] Global Network of Learning Cities in 2019.

Insect of the suborder Zygoptera in the order [[Odonata]], closely related to the [[Dragonfly|dragonfly]]. Damselflies are usually smaller and slimmer than dragonflies, and most species fold their wings along the body at rest. About 3,300 species are known, and the group has existed since the Late Jurassic and is found on every continent except [[Antarctica]]. All damselflies are predators. Their aquatic nymphs live in habitats from acidic [[Bog|bogs]] to [[Pond|ponds]], [[Lake|lakes]] and [[River|rivers]], and their presence suggests relatively unpolluted water. Males are often more brightly colored than females, and mating pairs form a shape known as a "heart" or "wheel".

Canadian and American actor, comedian, writer and musician. An original cast member of [[Saturday Night Live]] on [[NBC]] from 1975 to 1979, he co-founded the Blues Brothers act with [[John Belushi]]. He starred in *The Blues Brothers* (1980) and co-wrote and starred in *Ghostbusters* (1984). He was nominated for an Academy Award for *Driving Miss Daisy* (1989). He co-founded the House of Blues chain of music venues and the Crystal Head [[Vodka]] brand.

American former professional football quarterback in the [[National Football League]]. Marino played college football at the University of Pittsburgh and was the last quarterback taken in the first round of the 1983 draft. Known for his quick release and powerful arm, he played for the Miami Dolphins, leading them to the playoffs ten times and to one Super Bowl (XIX). In 1984 he was named NFL Most Valuable Player after setting single-season records of 5,084 passing yards and 48 touchdown passes. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2005.

Swiss mathematician and physicist, one of the many prominent mathematicians of the Bernoulli family of [[Basel]]. Born in Groningen in the Netherlands, he is remembered for applying mathematics to mechanics, especially fluid mechanics, and for pioneering work in probability and statistics. His name is commemorated in [[Bernoulli's principle]], an example of [[Conservation of energy|conservation of energy]] that describes the mechanism behind the carburetor and the airplane wing. His chief work, *Hydrodynamica* (1738), derived its results from a single principle. He was the son of [[Johann Bernoulli]] and nephew of [[Jacob Bernoulli]], and a close friend of [[Leonhard Euler]]. He was professor of mathematics in St. Petersburg from 1724 until 1733, then returned to Basel.

American frontiersman and pioneer, one of the first folk heroes of the United States. In 1775 he blazed the Wilderness Road into [[Kentucky]] and founded Boonesborough, one of the first English-speaking settlements west of the [[Appalachian Mountains]]. He served in the [[American Revolutionary War]] and was captured by the Shawnee before escaping. Heavily in debt from Kentucky land speculation, he resettled in [[Missouri]] in 1799. Tall tales and fiction later made him a legendary figure.

English actor known for playing the secret agent James Bond. He played Bond in *Casino Royale* (2006), *Quantum of Solace* (2008), *Skyfall* (2012), *Spectre* (2015) and *No Time to Die* (2021). He trained at the National Youth Theatre and the Guildhall School of Music and Drama in [[London]]. His breakthrough came in the drama serial *Our Friends in the North* (1996). He also played detective Benoit Blanc in the *Knives Out* films, and he was nominated for a Golden Globe for *Queer* (2024).

English actor known for intense method acting in auteur films. He has won a record three [[Academy Awards]] for Best Actor, for *My Left Foot* (1989), *There Will Be Blood* (2007) and *Lincoln* (2012). He also won four BAFTAs and two Golden Globe Awards, and he was knighted in 2014 for services to drama. He retired from acting from 1997 to 2000 to become an apprentice shoemaker in Italy, and again from 2017 to 2024. He returned in *Anemone* (2025), which he co-wrote and which was directed by his son Ronan.

English writer, journalist, merchant and spy. He is known for the novels *Robinson Crusoe* (1719), *Moll Flanders* (1722) and *Roxana: The Fortunate Mistress* (1724), and is seen as one of the earliest proponents of the English novel. *Robinson Crusoe* had run through four editions by the end of 1719, and its many imitations gave the name Robinsonade to a genre. Defoe also wrote many political tracts, was often in trouble with the authorities, and spent a period in prison. He traded in hosiery, woolen goods and wine, but debts forced him into bankruptcy in 1692. Later he served William III as a secret agent.
